papers.title: Childhood and adolescent changes in sleep spindle trends across the night.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Detected and measured sleep spindles in central and frontal EEG across 1944 nights from 97 participants aged 6-18 to characterize cycle trends in spindle density, frequency, amplitude, and duration. Spindle density and duration increased steeply between cycles 1 and 2, with the increase diminishing with age, and frequency trends shifted from increases across cycles in children to u-shaped in older adolescents, suggesting homeostatic-to-circadian and maturational influences.

papers.title: Collapse of local circuit integrated information Φ during NREM sleep.
papers.summary: Tested the Integrated Information Theory prediction at the neural circuit level by quantifying integrated information Φ within local cortical circuits across wakefulness, REM, and NREM sleep. Found that local-circuit Φ decreased during NREM compared to wakefulness (and frontal cortex REM), especially during OFF-periods, supporting the hypothesis that loss of consciousness corresponds to collapse of integrated information in local circuits.

papers.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state eyes-open EEG in natural short sleepers (≤6 h/night without subjective daytime dysfunction) versus recommended-length sleepers, finding higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents (especially occipital) in short sleepers, with a trend toward increasing exponents over time. These markers suggest increased drowsiness and less stable wakefulness under low stimulation, possibly masked by perceived resilience to short sleep.

papers.title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events.
papers.summary: Recorded from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients learning a concept-based story and found reactivation of concept neurons during slow-wave sleep, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. The temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of events in the story, indicating human concept-cell reactivation reflects semantic content rather than event order.

papers.title: Sleep changes what memories become: Post-learning sleep reduces forgetting following delayed reactivation.
papers.summary: Examined whether a post-learning nap influences declarative memory one week later and after delayed reactivation across two studies. A short nap alone showed no advantage at delayed testing, but after a reminder reactivation, napped participants showed less forgetting than awake participants, with slow-wave sleep duration, slow-oscillation activity, and fast spindles associated with better post-reactivation memory.

papers.title: Periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs) during NREM sleep before nocturnal seizures in temporal and extratemporal lobe epilepsy: An exploratory quantitative EEG study.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed 711 periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs) in 68 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients to compare spectral power between temporal and extratemporal lobe epilepsy before nocturnal seizures. Relative PGND delta power was higher in extratemporal than temporal lobe epilepsy (51.6% vs 45.1%), a widespread difference with modest discrimination (AUC 0.669), suggesting localization-related differences rather than a preictal biomarker.

papers.title: Protocol-aware dual-view single-channel EEG sleep staging with improved N1 discrimination on public sleep-EDF and SHHS benchmarks.
papers.summary: Developed DualViewSeqSleepNet, a protocol-aware single-channel EEG sleep staging model combining raw-waveform and spectral encoders with cross-epoch aggregation and N1-aware auxiliary loss. On Sleep-EDF it reached macro-F1 0.821, accuracy 0.869, and kappa 0.808, improving N1 F1 from 0.506 to 0.535; on SHHS-1 it achieved macro-F1 0.791 and accuracy 0.854 without retuning.

papers.title: High-Density EEG Signatures of Cataplexy in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: Using 128-channel EEG polysomnography in 10 drug-free adults with narcolepsy type 1 across 73 cataplexy epochs, the study found cataplexy exhibits a hybrid REM-like/wake-like spectral signature with mixed wake-, REM-, and N1-like hypnodensity probabilities. Signatures varied more between than within participants, supporting a dissociated hybrid brain state distinct from direct wake-to-REM transition.

papers.title: BDNF-mediated amelioration of sleep disruption-induced behavioral disorders by Ginkgo biloba.
papers.summary: In a rat model of multiple-platform sleep disruption, intraperitoneal Ginkgo biloba extract (250 mg/kg) improved Barnes maze learning (probe-day latency 71±11 s to 38±8 s) and prevented the sleep-disruption-induced hippocampal BDNF decrease (381±17 to 557±27 pg/ml). Ginkgo biloba treatment also improved memory and reduced anxiety.

papers.title: Actimetry-Derived Sleep and Circadian Parameters in a Population-Based Sample from São Paulo: Findings from the EPISONO Cohort.
papers.summary: Derived actimetry-based sleep, circadian, light exposure, and skin temperature parameters from 404 EPISONO cohort participants in São Paulo to establish urban reference values and model demographic and lifestyle effects. Older age, female sex, lower socioeconomic status, obesity, and season were associated with distinct differences in sleep timing, rhythm stability, fragmentation, and light exposure.

papers.title: Combination acetazolamide and supplemental oxygen markedly improves ventilatory control instability and OSA severity.
papers.summary: In a randomized single-blind crossover trial of 22 participants with moderate-severe OSA, combination acetazolamide plus supplemental oxygen markedly reduced loop gain (-0.26) and flow-based AHI by -23.3/h (-55.2%), roughly halving AHI though not superior to acetazolamide alone for AHI.

papers.title: Circadian Disruption and Chrono-rehabilitation After Spinal Cord Injury.
papers.journal: Topics in spinal cord injury rehabilitation
papers.summary: This review proposes a chronobiological framework for spinal cord injury rehabilitation, arguing that circadian disruption (clock gene dysregulation, inverted melatonin rhythms, blunted thermoregulation, lost autonomic timing) impairs neuroplasticity and recovery. It recommends actigraphy-based sleep-wake assessment, timed bright light therapy, dosed melatonin, and scheduling therapy during peak performance windows, while noting limited direct SCI trial evidence.

papers.title: Impact of intermittent hypoxia on drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters and drug pharmacokinetics: an underestimated concern in obstructive sleep apnea patients?
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that intermittent hypoxia and inflammation in obstructive sleep apnea alter drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters (DMETs), potentially changing pharmacokinetics and drug response, and proposes priority research areas to characterize these effects.

papers.title: Effects of Circadian Disruption and Chronotype on Postural Stability During Quiet Stance.
papers.summary: Examined how circadian regularity, misalignment parameters (composite phase deviation, interdaily stability, intradaily variability), and chronotype relate to postural stability during quiet stance in 39 healthy adults using force-platform center-of-pressure measures and recurrence quantification analysis. Greater circadian disruption and later chronotype were associated with greater postural instability, including increased sway and higher laminarity and trapping time.

papers.title: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological management of sleep disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and network meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (N=936) compared pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for sleep disturbances in Alzheimer's disease. Non-pharmacological approaches (walking, bright light therapy, NITE-AD) reduced nocturnal awakenings, while dual orexin receptor antagonists improved total sleep time and Z-drugs reduced sleep fragmentation but with safety concerns, supporting non-pharmacological treatment first.

papers.title: Preserved social development but impaired executive function in a Shank3 -deficient rat model of Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study transferred a targeted Shank3 mutation onto the Long-Evans rat strain and longitudinally assessed Shank3-deficient rats from infancy to adulthood. Despite profound loss of Shank3 protein, rats showed normal sensorimotor development and intact social preference, but adults displayed rapid error-prone responding in touchscreen discrimination and reversal learning, indicating executive dysfunction as a key consequence of Shank3 loss.

papers.title: EEG biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases: Machine learning applications and clinical trial insights.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from 226 studies on EEG-based machine learning and AI approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and patient stratification across neurodegenerative diseases. It reports that spectral power, event-related potentials, and connectivity are the main features with support vector machines and neural networks as primary classifiers, while highlighting persistent challenges of small samples and limited clinical validation.

papers.title: Transformer-based EEG source imaging localizes pathological high-frequency oscillations in focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: The authors introduce TH-DeepSIF, a transformer-based deep source-imaging framework trained on neural mass model simulations to localize high-frequency oscillations from scalp EEG in focal epilepsy. In 20 drug-resistant epilepsy patients, pathological spike ripples localized with a median error of 10.9 mm and specificity of 0.883 relative to resection regions, and with 2.41 mm error to seizure onset zones in six patients with intracranial EEG.

papers.title: Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking environmental noise, particularly road traffic noise, to cardiovascular and metabolic disease, including ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, and diabetes. It describes a convergent pathway of stress-responsive neural activation, sympathetic and HPA axis activity, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and argues that noise remains absent from cardiovascular risk assessment and mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Seizure-like behaviors in a mutant mouse with increased calpain-dependent cleavage of αII-spectrin.
papers.summary: In heterozygous Sptan1 R1098Q mice, a novel model of spectrin-related neurodevelopmental disease, the authors combined video-EEG, gait analysis, and a handling-induced seizure susceptibility paradigm and found pronounced ataxia, increased delta/theta power, and spike-wave discharges. Seizure-like motor responses occurred in nearly all mutants but did not coincide with cortical ictal EEG activity, demonstrating a dissociation between behavioral seizure-like events and cortical ictal correlates.

papers.title: Comparative outcomes following virtual reality-assisted and traditional supplementary exercise programs and usual training on balance, sprint performance, and resting-state EEG in youth academy football players.
papers.summary: This randomized study compared an eight-week virtual reality-assisted supplementary exercise program, a traditional supplementary program, and usual training in 39 youth-academy football players, assessing balance, 30-m sprint, and resting-state EEG. The virtual reality group showed greater baseline-adjusted improvements in two-leg, dominant-leg, and non-dominant-leg balance than both other groups, with only exploratory EEG differences in anterior spectral power and anterior-central synchronization.

papers.title: Comparative efficacy of different digital technologies in adults with insomnia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
keywords: digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia
papers.summary: This Bayesian network meta-analysis of 26 RCTs (6,353 adults with insomnia) evaluated eight digital interventions and found that digital interventions significantly reduced Insomnia Severity Index, improved Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and shortened sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset. Digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia ranked favorably, particularly for sleep onset latency, though sparse direct comparative evidence limited certainty for some interventions and outcomes.

papers.title: Temporal dissociation across the eye-brain-muscle cascade delineates a preparation window before muscle activation in subacute stroke.
papers.summary: Thirty subacute stroke survivors and 30 healthy controls performed a nine-grid reaching task with synchronous eye-tracking, EEG, and surface EMG, revealing stepwise delays in first fixation and muscle activation onset that bracketed a cortical preparation window. A random-forest classifier using gaze-timing features discriminated the occurrence of instructed reaching actions with an AUC of 0.973 and accuracy of 0.918.

papers.title: TToTP model: An automated detection of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia using Tesla Tree of Thought Pattern with EEG signals.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a self-organized explainable feature engineering model incorporating a novel Tesla Tree of Thought Pattern feature extraction function, cumulative weighted iterative neighborhood component analysis, tkNN classification, and iterative majority voting to detect Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls from EEG. The model achieved over 99% classification accuracy on a public EEG dementia dataset and generated a cortical channel map.

papers.title: Association between exertional dyspnea and insomnia in a population-based cohort.
papers.summary: In a population-based cohort of 1,221 adults, insomnia (ISI ≥8, ISI ≥15, and subthreshold/clinical categories) was significantly associated with higher odds of exertional dyspnea (mMRC ≥1) after adjustment, including in participants with unexplained dyspnea.

papers.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury following cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: integration of circadian rhythm and anesthetic factors to develop and validate a predictive model at 7 days.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 298 patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass developed and internally validated a nomogram predicting postoperative acute kidney injury (incidence 27.52%), incorporating circadian rhythm and anesthesia-related variables with an AUC of 0.796 in training and 0.776 in validation.

papers.title: A Nationally Representative Study of Complementary and Alternative Medicine Therapies in relation to Sleep Duration and Insomnia Symptoms among US Adults.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using nationally representative 2012 NHIS data from 30,405 US adults, any complementary and alternative medicine use was associated with higher prevalence of short sleep duration (aPR 1.11) and insomnia symptoms (aPR 1.56), with the strongest insomnia association for meditation/guided imagery/progressive relaxation.

papers.title: Nocturnal Sweating in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 10 studies and exploratory meta-analysis of three comparative studies found nocturnal sweating was not consistently associated with OSA severity indices; the pooled odds ratio for increased nocturnal sweating in OSA was non-significant (OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.87-3.92, I2=91.7%), though sweating may reflect hypoxemic burden and sympathetic activation and improved with PAP therapy.

papers.title: Integrated rehabilitation for post-stroke anxiety: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In this multicenter randomized controlled trial of 188 post-stroke anxiety patients, an integrated rehabilitation program (rTMS, acupuncture, and Chinese herbal medicine added to standard care) produced greater HAM-A reductions at Week 4 (between-group difference 2.49 points) that were maintained at Week 12, with supportive benefits in sleep quality, cognition, and upper-extremity motor function.

papers.title: Enabling Rapid Calibration of BCI Systems that Detect Movement-Related Cortical Potentials in Children with Cerebral Palsy.
papers.summary: Using EEG from 27 sessions in four children with cerebral palsy, a Bi-LSTM framework achieved 91% accuracy with cross-subject cumulative learning without within-session calibration and 93% with transfer learning plus minimal calibration, substantially reducing BCI calibration requirements.

papers.title: Perioperative esketamine is associated with attenuated sleep deprivation-related cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective biomarker cohort study of the ferroptosis-neuroinflammation axis.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: In a retrospective biomarker cohort of 398 older adults undergoing major non-cardiac surgery, perioperative esketamine was associated with lower odds of early postoperative cognitive decline in sleep-deprived patients (adjusted OR 0.49) and with attenuation of a peripheral ferroptosis-related/inflammatory phenotype (lower 4-HNE, MDA, ACSL4, IL-6 and higher GSH, GPX4, SLC7A11). An exploratory redox score was independently associated with cognitive decline, with a model-based mediated proportion of 54%.

papers.title: Metrics Reflecting Cumulative Exposure to Nocturnal Hypoxia Demonstrate Promising Performance in Distinguishing between Moderate and Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In 30 patients with moderate or severe OSA assessed by actigraphy and nocturnal oximetry, cumulative time with SpO2 below 90% and hypoxic burden remained independently associated with severe disease after BMI adjustment, with AUCs of 0.86 and 0.84 respectively, outperforming desaturation frequency (AUC 0.78).

papers.title: Culturally Adapting a Behavioral Sleep Intervention for Older Korean Immigrants: A Community-Engaged Refinement Study.
papers.summary: Refined a CBT-I-based behavioral sleep program (SLEEP-OK) for older Korean immigrants using participant and stakeholder feedback across five in-person sessions, making both surface- and deep-structure cultural adaptations. All participants completed the program with high acceptability and engagement, and sleep educators found adapted sessions easy to deliver.

papers.title: Dupilumab for Moderate-to-Severe Chronic Prurigo Nodularis: A Retrospective Real-World Study of Effectiveness, Safety, and Prolonged Dosing Intervals.
papers.summary: Retrospective single-center real-world study of dupilumab in 26 adults with moderate-to-severe chronic prurigo nodularis found that 59% achieved a ≥4-point WI-NRS itch reduction and 45% achieved IGA PN-S 0/1 at week 24, with uncommon adverse events. Prolonged dosing intervals were maintained in five of nine controlled responders, and psychiatric comorbidity was associated with lower odds of itch response.

papers.title: Associations Between Marital Status and 24-Hr Movement Behaviors Among Older Adults: A Compositional Data Analysis With Gender-Stratified Findings.
papers.journal: Journal of aging and physical activity
papers.summary: Compositional data analysis of accelerometer-derived 24-hour movement behaviors in 814 older adults from SHARE Wave 8 found that not being partnered was associated with lower moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and higher sedentary behavior. Gender-stratified analyses indicated these patterns were more pronounced among unpartnered men.

papers.title: Mandibular advancement device vs continuous positive airway pressure in obstructive sleep apnea: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1244 participants) comparing mandibular advancement devices with CPAP in obstructive sleep apnea found CPAP superior for polysomnographic outcomes (SpO2, ODI, arousal index), whereas MAD showed significantly greater adherence and modest blood pressure reductions; baseline AHI moderated treatment effects.

papers.title: Short-term multidimensional effects of continuous positive airway pressure in patients with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome: a single-center retrospective study.
papers.summary: Single-center retrospective study of 89 OSAHS patients found that adding CPAP to lifestyle intervention for 12 weeks yielded a higher overall response rate (92.86% vs 42.55%) and greater improvements in AHI, lowest oxygen saturation, sleep quality, inflammatory cytokines, hemorheology, endothelial function, and quality of life than lifestyle intervention alone.

papers.title: Acupuncture and related needling in sports-related knee rehabilitation: a narrative review of neurophysiological mechanisms and assessment methods.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes indirect evidence on manual acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and trigger point dry needling as adjuncts in sports-related knee rehabilitation, grouping proposed mechanisms into cortical, corticospinal/spinal-reflexive, and peripheral muscular levels. The authors report that clinical studies suggest possible improvements in pain, swelling, range of motion, function, and neuromuscular performance, but note that direct evidence in sports-related knee injury populations remains limited and the framework is hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: A dynamic network analysis of anxiety-related distress within a quality-of-life framework among adults undergoing chemotherapy.
papers.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial data used longitudinal network analysis in 390 adults aged 50 and older assessed across six time points before and during chemotherapy to locate anxiety-related distress (worry and tension) within the EORTC QLQ quality-of-life framework. Worry emerged as a central bridging node, positively associated with depressed mood, trouble sleeping, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and financial difficulties, and financial difficulties predicted higher subsequent worry but lower subsequent tension.

papers.title: Mapping the global landscape of research on primary and secondary headaches from 2000 to 2025: a bibliometric analysis.
authors: Wellington Luiz de Oliveira da Rosa
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis of 40,441 PubMed records on primary and secondary headaches from 2000 to 2025 mapped output, citation impact, collaboration, co-citation, and MeSH term bursts, finding annual output rising from 747 to 2,522 articles and a shift from triptans toward calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) therapies. Tension-type headache was underrepresented relative to its prevalence, and the dental interface (temporomandibular disorders, bruxism, orofacial pain) appeared in only 1.3% of articles.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
